description: Imports Shopify store data — orders, customers, products and variants, collections, inventory, fulfillments, refunds, returns, disputes, subscription contracts and their metafields — from the Shopify GraphQL Admin API.

placeholders.store: the `store` field of each entry in the `stores` endpoint-config list (the myshopify subdomain, e.g. 'mystore'); a single capture may configure several stores and therefore several base URLs at once

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment — /admin/api/2026-01/graphql.json, from the connector constant VERSION in graphql/common.py

credentialModes.name: Private App Credentials (custom app admin access token)
Client Credentials (Shopify Dev Dashboard custom app, client_credentials grant)

artifacts: Shopify BulkOperation jobs (gid://shopify/BulkOperation/<n>) created per bulk-query stream slice, and the JSONL result files Shopify stores for them
continuity.ourSideLoss: A completed bulk job's result URL is a short-lived signed link and the job itself can reach EXPIRED status, so a slice whose result is not downloaded promptly must be re-run. Nothing is permanently lost — the window is simply re-queried from the stored cursor.
continuity.resumeWindow: Indefinite for correctness: state is a datetime cursor per stream per store, and the next run resumes from it by re-querying updated_at windows. Long pauses only mean more windows to walk (window_size defaults to 30 days).
continuity.notes: No server-side subscription, slot, or consumer group exists on the customer side — nothing accrues on their infra while we are stopped. The only server-side artifacts are Shopify's own bulk-operation jobs, which are NOT cancelled on shutdown; instead, on the next Open the connector queries bulkOperations(query: "status:RUNNING type:QUERY") and cancels whatever it finds, because Shopify caps a shop+app at 5 concurrent bulk query jobs. A crashed run therefore leaves running jobs occupying that cap until the next start; jobs left by a *different* app cannot be cancelled and hard-block submission.

configFields.name: stores
configFields.description: One or more Shopify stores to capture. Each store requires its own credentials. Minimum length 1.

configFields.name: stores[].store
configFields.description: Shopify store name — the prefix of the admin URL, e.g. 'mystore' for mystore.myshopify.com. Must be unique across the list.

configFields.name: stores[].credentials.credentials_title
configFields.description: Discriminator selecting the credential variant: "Private App Credentials" or "Client Credentials".

configFields.name: stores[].credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Admin API access token for the store (Private App Credentials variant).

configFields.name: stores[].credentials.client_id
configFields.description: Custom-app client id, exchanged for a ~24h access token via the client_credentials grant (Client Credentials variant).

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Data generated before this is not replicated. Defaults to 30 days before the present.

configFields.name: advanced.window_size
configFields.description: ISO 8601 duration bounding each incremental slice of the bulk-query streams (e.g. P30D, PT6H). Default P30D, minimum 1 minute.

configFields.name: advanced.should_use_composite_key
configFields.description: Whether collection keys include the store identifier (/_meta/store). Default true; forced false when migrating a legacy single-store config.

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO 8601 interval between updates for this binding. Connector default PT5M for incremental streams, PT15M for the staff_members snapshot.

configFields.name: schedule
configFields.description: Cron expression that automatically re-backfills this binding. Connector default is empty except disputes, which ships "55 23 * * *".

discovery.method: Fixed shipped list, then filtered per store at connect time by a GraphQL `{ currentAppInstallation { accessScopes { handle } } }` query and, for custom-app tokens, a `{ shop { plan { displayName partnerDevelopment shopifyPlus } } }` query.
discovery.querySketch: currentAppInstallation.accessScopes.handle -> set of granted scope handles; shop.plan -> PII gating (Basic/Starter plans cannot read customers, orders, fulfillment_orders) and Plus/Advanced gating. A stream is offered only if at least one of its QUALIFYING_SCOPES is granted on at least one configured store.
excludes: streams whose QUALIFYING_SCOPES are disjoint from the granted scopes
customers, orders, fulfillment_orders when a custom-app token is used on a Basic or Starter plan
staff_members unless the shop is Shopify Plus, Advanced, or a partner development store
discovery.allowlist: The 27 INCREMENTAL_RESOURCES plus the single FULL_REFRESH_RESOURCES entry (staff_members) shipped in resources.py — discovery only ever narrows this list.

incremental.querySketch: POST /admin/api/2026-01/graphql.json with a bulk-job submit mutation: `mutation { bulkOperationRunQuery(query: """{ abandonedCheckouts(query: "updated_at:>='<start>' AND updated_at:<='<end>'") { edges { node { id legacyResourceId createdAt updatedAt <resource fields> } } } }""", groupObjects: true) { bulkOperation { id status url errorCode } userErrors { field message code } } }`. The returned BulkOperation gid is then polled with `{ node(id: "<gid>") { ... on BulkOperation { status url errorCode } } }` until status == COMPLETED, and the JSONL file at the returned `url` is downloaded and streamed line by line. Each invocation covers one [log_cursor, log_cursor+window_size] slice (window_size default P30D); the cursor advances to the window end.

snapshot.querySketch: POST /admin/api/2026-01/graphql.json with an unfiltered Relay connection query: `{ staffMembers(first: 250, after: "<cursor>") { edges { node { id active accountType email firstName lastName isShopOwner ... } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }`. StaffMember has no updatedAt and staffMembers cannot filter or sort by date, so the full set is re-read each snapshot.

authTierRationale: The easiest mode is Private App Credentials: the merchant creates a custom app in their own Shopify admin, grants the listed read_* scopes, and pastes the single Admin API access token (shpat_*) into stores[].credentials.access_token — one self-serve secret, no app registration on our side and no refresh token. The second mode (Client Credentials) is T2_BYO_APP: the user must register their own app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard and supply client_id + client_secret, which the CDK exchanges for a ~24h token at https://{store}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token and refreshes at 75% of lifetime. There is NO hosted-control-plane OAuth: ConnectorSpec is emitted with oauth2=None and a code comment states the authorization-code OAUTH2_SPEC was deliberately removed pending app approval and UI support for credentials inside array items. So no T3_BYO_REFRESH mode exists either.

unionMisfits.description: The dominant pull mechanism is a Shopify bulk operation: a GraphQL mutation SUBMITS a job, a second GraphQL query POLLS `node(id:)` until COMPLETED (backing off 1s→2s, warning past 6h), and the payload is then fetched by an unauthenticated-style GET of a signed JSONL result URL returned in the job details — three different requests against two different hosts, with a job lifecycle (CREATED/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED/EXPIRED/CANCELED), a per-shop concurrency cap of 5, and cancel-on-start reconciliation. No PullSpec member expresses submit→poll→download. It has been forced into kind: "query" with the whole lifecycle described in querySketch and paginator "none", which loses the fact that a failed poll or an expired URL — not a paginator bug — is how this stream silently stops producing data.

poll.requestSketch: query { node(id: <jobId>) { ... on BulkOperation { status url errorCode } } }
poll.backoff: 1s doubling to a 2s ceiling, no overall timeout; warns after 6h

fetch.recordAssembly: parent/child flattening on the `__parentId` field — child lines (metafields, scheduled changes, …) are appended to the preceding parent line

unionMisfits.description: One capture is multi-tenant: `stores` is a LIST, each entry carrying its own store subdomain AND its own credentials object, and every binding fans out into one subtask per store with its own HTTP session, rate limiter, TokenSource and bulk-job manager. The schema models a single baseUrl and a flat, connector-level set of credential alternatives, so it cannot say 'N base URLs, each paired with one of these credential modes'. Credential mode may even differ per store (one access token, one client-credentials pair).

tenancy.documentKeyDiscriminator: /_meta/store, prepended to every collection key when advanced.should_use_composite_key is true

unionMisfits.description: Bulk-query streams have NO backfill leg at all — resources.py sets use_backfill = not SHOULD_USE_BULK_QUERIES, so their ResourceState carries only `inc`. The historical sweep and the ongoing leg are literally the same call, which walks fixed advanced.window_size windows forward from start_date. Reporting backfill: null is correct but reads as 'no historical data', which is wrong.

pull.unifiedSemantics: windowed forward walk from start_date; the same spec serves history and steady state

unionMisfits.description: The cron on a binding does not drive a fetch — it re-initialises the binding (ResourceConfigWithSchedule.schedule: 'Schedule to automatically rebackfill this binding'). disputes ships "55 23 * * *" because the disputes connection can only be filtered on initiatedAt, so updates to already-captured disputes are invisible to the incremental leg and are only recovered by re-reading everything nightly. The schema's Schedule union has no way to mark a schedule as 'reset state and re-read' rather than 'poll now', which is a materially different cost and correctness story.

Two pagination levels are collapsed into one. Inside a single fetch_page invocation the connector follows the Relay pageInfo.endCursor; but the token it hands back to the runtime is a DATETIME string (the last-seen cursor value), and the next invocation restarts Relay paging from scratch with that datetime as the new lower bound after ~5 minutes of wall clock. Reporting only the cursor paginator hides that resumption is time-based and therefore re-reads the tail of the previous page. The unsorted variant (disputes, locations, inventory_items) is different again — it returns the Relay endCursor itself as the page token, one page per invocation.

outer.emittedEvery: 1000 documents, or after 5 minutes of runtime

unionMisfits.description: The stream list is static, but the SET a given capture sees is narrowed at connect time by granted scopes and shop plan — and, one level deeper, the FIELDS inside each query are spliced in or out per store by CONDITIONAL_FIELDS predicates (e.g. disputes' whole disputeEvidence block requires read_shopify_payments_dispute_evidences, a scope distinct from the one gating the stream). The schema can express a narrowed stream list only via `discovery`, and has nowhere at all to record per-store field-level variation, so two captures of the same 'stream' can carry different columns.

The key is config-dependent, not fixed: advanced.should_use_composite_key toggles every collection key between [/_meta/store, /id] and [/id] (legacy single-store captures are auto-migrated to the latter), and changing it requires re-discovery plus a dataflow reset. A single primaryKey list cannot express that. The composite form is reported here because it is the default for new captures.

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No connector-level default headers are set. Requests carry only the auth header injected by the CDK plus whatever aiohttp adds; the GraphQL body is sent via the CDK's json= argument, so no explicit Content-Type is written in connector code.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: There is no connector-wide schedule. Every schedule is per-binding initial_config (PT5M incremental, PT15M snapshot), so the connector-level default is genuinely null.
abstained.streams[*].pull.<spec>.recordsPath / par: Not applicable: every request is a POST to the single /graphql.json endpoint with the selection expressed in the GraphQL document body. There are no addressable per-stream REST paths, no query params, and no envelope record path other than data.<QUERY_ROOT>.edges[].node (non-bulk) or one JSON object per line of the bulk result file.
abstained.streams[0].cursorField: abandoned_checkouts declares SORT_KEY = CREATED_AT, so get_cursor_value() would read createdAt — but it is a bulk-query stream, and on the bulk path the log cursor is advanced to the window end without consulting get_cursor_value, while the query itself filters on updated_at. Reported as updatedAt (the field that actually bounds each slice); the createdAt declaration is currently dead on this path and could change behaviour if the stream ever moved off bulk queries.
abstained.streams[*].pull.<spec>.incrementalParam: No such param exists. The incremental bound is interpolated into the GraphQL search-syntax string (updated_at:>='<iso8601>' AND updated_at:<='<iso8601>', or initiated_at for disputes) inside the query document, not sent as an HTTP parameter.
abstained.credentialModes[1].scheme.authUrl: None exists. The authorization-code flow was deliberately removed (see the TODO in models.py) and ConnectorSpec is emitted with oauth2=None, so there is no user-facing authorize URL — only the per-store token endpoint used by the client_credentials grant.
abstained.credentialModes[1].scheme.scopes: The listed scopes are the connector's documented requirement (models.py `scopes`), which was written for the removed authorization-code flow. The client_credentials token request built by the CDK sends only grant_type/client_id/client_secret — no scope parameter — so these are scopes the user must grant on the app, not scopes transmitted at token exchange.
abstained.streams[*].supportedSyncModes / writeDis: Neither concept is named in the code; both are inferred. 'incremental' is inferred from the presence of ResourceState.Incremental cursors, 'merge' from the keyed collections plus the default _meta op of 'u', and 'snapshot_with_tombstone' for staff_members from the explicit tombstone document with op='d' passed to open_binding.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.paginator.cursorPath: Written with a <queryRoot> placeholder rather than a literal path: the envelope field under `data` is the stream's QUERY_ROOT and differs per stream (orders, products, collections, inventoryItems, customers, locations, disputes, abandonedCheckouts, subscriptionContracts, staffMembers), and the response model is built dynamically by create_response_data_model.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.paginator (b: Recorded as type 'none' because the bulk result file is streamed in full with no page token. The real bound is temporal (advanced.window_size, default P30D). Calling this 'none' should not be read as 'unbounded'.
